long_biography.plain_text:
Property developer Tore Solbakken sought to turn Oslo's Torshovtoppen site into a neighbourhood designed for different generations. Working with planning consultancy Urba, his team used a pilot project to explore housing suited to older residents and gathered local input before submitting its proposals.

After the municipality rejected the initial plan, Solbakken and Bastia appointed new architects to rework it. The revised proposal increased green space and retained more existing buildings. Alongside the longer planning process, the team sought permission to put older buildings into temporary use, with the aim of keeping them occupied while their future was being decided.
